svg.title: Someone is seriously unwell or getting worse
svg.desc: Working three-part action card for a person who seems seriously unwell or is getting worse when the cause is unclear. Part one says to call Triple Zero if serious illness may be present or anyone thinks something is wrong, without waiting for a diagnosis, a severe sign or every listed sign. It gives immediate exits for abnormal or uncertain breathing and life-threatening bleeding. It shows observable breathing, response, skin, whole-body and concern cues without creating an all-clear when none is noticed. Part two routes immediate danger, life-threatening bleeding, abnormal or uncertain breathing, normal breathing while unresponsive, seizure and known causes to existing Chapter 6 actions. The recovery-position route is limited to an adult or child aged one year or older; infant side-position mechanics are not shown. Part three repeats the Triple Zero and breathing exits, gives a comfortable lying-or-chair choice for a conscious person with no matching condition-specific position, uses the matching condition card for supplies and medicines, prevents a generic food or drink instruction, protects against heat or cold according to what is found, and requires continuous observation and reporting of change. It does not diagnose shock or sepsis, set a lone-rescuer priority between simultaneous life threats, teach physical handling, or replace Triple Zero or a condition-specific card.
svg.text: SERIOUSLY UNWELL — CAUSE UNCLEAR
WORKING CARD · PART 1 OF 3
WARNING — CLINICAL + PRACTICAL REVIEW NEEDED
Estimates: source wording 95%; cross-condition limits 75%; layout 60%.
These do not estimate safety, diagnosis, treatment, recovery or survival.
Do not delay 000 while trying to name the illness or count every sign.
Suspect serious illness—or think “something is wrong”? Call 000. Follow the call-taker.
CALL 000 IF SERIOUS ILLNESS MAY BE PRESENT
Or if the person, a parent, a carer or you think “something is wrong”.
Signs are examples, not a checklist. None can prove the person is safe.
BREATHING
Struggling, fast, noisy or gasping; cannot
speak normally; lips or skin look blue
or grey.
RESPONSE
Hard to wake; unusually sleepy or floppy;
new confusion; collapse; seizure; getting
less responsive.
SKIN + CIRCULATION
Very pale, cool, sweaty, blotchy or newly
discoloured; a new widespread rash, or a
new rash with rapidly worsening illness.
WHOLE BODY + CONCERN
Very hot or very cold; shaking chills;
repeated vomiting; little or no urine;
“I do not feel right” or “I may die.”
NOT FIELD-APPROVED · USE ALL 3 PARTS
ABNORMAL OR UNCERTAIN BREATHING → CPR/AED NOW · LIFE-THREATENING BLEEDING → BLEEDING CARD
CALL — CHECK — USE THE RIGHT CARD
WORKING CARD · PART 2 OF 3
DANGER OR A LIFE THREAT OVERRIDES THIS CARD
Move only the minimum needed for current danger or lifesaving care.
Start CPR or bleeding care now. If both apply and you are alone, follow 000.
1 · CALL 000 NOW — ASK FOR AMBULANCE
Say that the person is seriously unwell and what you can see.
A capable helper calls while urgent care continues. Report every change.
No connection? Keep care going and use Chapter 3. Do not leave merely for signal.
2 · CHECK RESPONSE + NORMAL BREATHING
UNRESPONSIVE + not breathing normally, gasping or unsure:
Use the Chapter 6 CPR/AED cards now.
UNRESPONSIVE + breathing normally:
Use the age-one-plus recovery card; infant handling is not shown.
OBVIOUS LIFE-THREATENING BLEEDING:
Use the severe-bleeding card now while help is called.
3 · KNOWN CAUSE? USE ITS CHAPTER 6 CARD
Examples: anaphylaxis, asthma, seizure, stroke, heart problem, low glucose,
poisoning, burn, severe bleeding, heat or cold illness. Keep following 000.
NOT FIELD-APPROVED · USE ALL 3 PARTS · CAUSE UNCLEAR? CONTINUE TO PART 3
CALL 000 — CHECK BREATHING — PROTECT
WORKING CARD · PART 3 OF 3
ABNORMAL OR UNCERTAIN BREATHING → CPR/AED CARDS NOW
If conscious: lie down if comfortable; otherwise bring a chair to them.
Do not make them walk or routinely raise their legs.
The condition card/000 overrides. This is not an infant-handling method.
PROTECT BODY TEMPERATURE — MATCH WHAT YOU FIND
Feels very hot: do not add a blanket; remove excess clothing and use Chapter 5.
Cold or losing heat: insulate from the ground and add dry layers or a blanket.
Do not apply direct heat. Keep face and breathing visible.
Temperature care never replaces 000 or the known-cause treatment.
WITH A KIT / WITHOUT A KIT
With a kit: use only supplies named by the matching condition card or 000.
Without one: the same call, position, protection and breathing checks apply.
This generic card gives no food, drink, medicine, oxygen, stimulant or bush remedy.
KEEP WATCHING — REPORT CHANGE
Recheck response, normal breathing, bleeding, temperature and other change.
Abnormal or uncertain breathing goes to CPR. No fixed wait means “all clear.”
NOT FIELD-APPROVED · USE ALL 3 PARTS WITH THE CHAPTER WARNING
